rationale: Retain the existing Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI) canonical production company, retire the reciprocal Direct ChassisLink, Inc. seed identity, and complete the ownership chain. GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House closed their joint acquisition on December 13, 2022 and remain current owners with undisclosed percentages. Preserve Maersk, Littlejohn, EQT and Apollo as former owners; do not infer equal current ownership or the unresolved residual 2% in the 2019 Apollo transaction.

beforeImage.name: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI)
beforeImage.description: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. leases marine and domestic intermodal chassis used to move containerized freight between ports, rail terminals, and inland customer locations across the United States. Its customers include ocean carriers, railroads, motor carriers, beneficial cargo owners, and logistics intermediaries that depend on chassis availability for port and inland intermodal flows. The operating model is asset heavy and lease based, supported by a large fleet positioned at strategic port and rail locations rather than a brokerage model. Wren House states that DCLI operates more than 151,000 marine chassis and 121,000 domestic chassis and employs approximately 470 people, with headquarters in Charlotte. GIC, OMERS Infrastructure, and Wren House signed the acquisition of DCLI in 2022, and the platform has since remained under that consortium ownership. The investment gives Wren House exposure to essential equipment underpinning U.S. container logistics.

afterImage.name: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI)
afterImage.description: Direct ChassisLink, Inc. (DCLI) leases and manages marine and domestic intermodal chassis used to move containerized freight through more than 500 U.S. port and rail locations. The Charlotte-based platform serves ocean carriers, railroads, motor carriers, beneficial cargo owners, shippers and logistics providers and reports a fleet of approximately 290,000 chassis. GIC, OMERS Infrastructure and Wren House Infrastructure completed their joint acquisition on December 13, 2022; public materials identify the consortium as current but do not disclose member percentages, so no equal split is inferred. DCLI's former ownership chain includes Maersk, Littlejohn, EQT Infrastructure and Apollo-managed funds. The production database already redirects the retired duplicate production ID to this canonical company; this proposal also retires the reciprocal Direct ChassisLink, Inc. seed identity. No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.
